title: Metrics & Monitoring (Datadog)
summary: Collect, store and alert on millions of time series: agents that pre-aggregate, a write-optimised time-series store with compression and downsampling, a query engine, and an alerting pipeline that must keep working during incidents.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Ingest metrics (name + tags + timestamp + value) from hosts and apps
Query and graph over time ranges with aggregation (sum/avg/p99) by tag
Alert rules evaluated continuously; notify on-call
Ingest millions of points/s; recent data queryable within ~10 s
Alerting must stay up when the systems it monitors are down

blocks.title: Key insight
blocks.text: The killer is **cardinality** (number of unique series), not points. A tag like user_id multiplies series by millions.

items: Identify a series by hashing metric name + sorted tags; an inverted index maps tag=value → series ids for queries.
Write path: append to an in-memory head block per series (plus WAL), flush 2-hour immutable blocks to disk — an LSM-like design.
**Gorilla compression:** delta-of-delta timestamps and XOR-encoded floats compress points to ~1–2 bytes.
**Downsampling / rollups:** keep raw for ~2 weeks, 1-minute rollups for months, 1-hour for years (store min/max/sum/count, not just avg).

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Points are cheap; series are expensive. I'd cap cardinality per customer and reject unbounded tags like request ids.

items.title: Evaluate
items.text: Rules run every 10–60 s over a window (e.g. p99 latency > 500 ms for 5 min).

items.title: Stateful
items.text: Track pending → firing → resolved per rule and series to avoid flapping.

items.title: Route
items.text: Group, dedupe and route to on-call with escalation; silence during maintenance.

items.title: Independence
items.text: Run the alerting path on separate infrastructure; alert on missing data (dead man's switch).

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text: Evaluating alerts by querying the same storage cluster the dashboards hammer. During an incident everyone opens dashboards — alerts must not depend on that path.

items: Shard by series id hash; queries fan out to shards and merge partial aggregates.
Push (agents send) vs pull (Prometheus scrapes): push scales across networks; pull makes target health obvious.
Backpressure: agents buffer locally and drop the oldest points first if the gateway is unavailable.
Percentiles can't be averaged across hosts — store histograms/sketches (e.g. DDSketch) and merge them.

cols.title: Pull (Prometheus)
pros: Easy to tell when a target is down
cons: Hard across NAT/firewalls; service discovery needed

cols.title: Push (agents)
cons: Gateway must absorb bursts; harder to detect dead senders

items.title: HLD
items.text: Agents → gateway → Kafka → TSDB; query; alerts.

items.title: Deep dives
items.text: Compression, blocks, rollups; alert state machine.

items.q: How do you compute p99 across 1,000 hosts?
items.a: Each host ships a mergeable histogram/sketch; merge sketches, then read the quantile. Averaging p99s is wrong.

items.q: How do you handle a customer suddenly sending 100× series?
items.a: Per-tenant cardinality limits at ingest, with metrics about what was dropped.
Different stores (inverted index for logs, trace store keyed by trace id) but share agents, ingest and tags.

items: Series = name + tags; cardinality is the cost driver.
Head block in memory + WAL → immutable compressed blocks.
Alerting isolated from dashboards; alert on absent data.
